_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Djibouti covering Afar and Issa peoples, French Somaliland, strategic location at Bab el-Mandeb, independence 1977, foreign military bases, and the Guelleh era.

ethnic_groups.name: Somali (Issa)
ethnic_groups.notes: Issa clan of the Dir Somali; dominant in Djibouti City and south; historically linked to Somali clan system

ethnic_groups.name: Afar
ethnic_groups.notes: Cushitic-speaking pastoralists; northern and western regions; straddle Djibouti-Ethiopia-Eritrea borders; Sultanate of Tadjoura heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Yemeni and other Arab traders; commercial communities

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Somali minority clans)
ethnic_groups.notes: Gadabursi, Isaaq, and other Somali clans

current_leader.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Nephew of Hassan Gouled Aptidon; term limits removed 2010; re-elected 2021 for fifth term

former_leaders.name: Hassan Gouled Aptidon
former_leaders.notes: Founding president; Issa leader; single-party rule; Afar civil war 1991–1994

910.name: Ancient Peoples and Early Trade Routes
910.description: Ancient habitation at the crossroads of Africa and Arabia; early pastoralist cultures; rock art; links to the Land of Punt.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Rock Art and Pastoralists
sub_clusters.description: Neolithic rock art at Abourma and Balho; early Cushitic-speaking pastoralists in the Afar depression.

sub_clusters.name: Possible Link to Land of Punt
sub_clusters.description: Djibouti region as possible part of the ancient Land of Punt; Egyptian trade expeditions for myrrh, frankincense, and gold.

sub_clusters.name: Afar and Issa Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Afar and Issa (Dir Somali) peoples establish pastoral and trading communities; Afar dominance in the north, Issa in the south.

920.name: Islamic Sultanates and Trade
920.description: Islamisation of the region; Ifat and Adal sultanates; Djibouti as part of broader Horn of Africa Islamic polities; Red Sea trade.

sub_clusters.name: Islamisation of the Afar and Issa
sub_clusters.description: Spread of Islam through Arab traders and scholars; conversion of Afar and Issa peoples; mosque construction.

sub_clusters.name: Adal Sultanate Influence
sub_clusters.description: Djibouti region under influence of Adal Sultanate; Ahmed Gran's jihad against Ethiopia; Zeila as major port.

930.name: Ottoman and Egyptian Influence
930.description: Ottoman Empire and Egyptian Khedivate contest control of the Red Sea coast; Afar sultanates maintain local autonomy.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Red Sea Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Ottoman influence on the Red Sea coast; Afar sultanate of Tadjoura maintains semi-autonomy under Ottoman suzerainty.

sub_clusters.name: Egyptian Khedivate and Regional Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: Egyptian expansion into Horn of Africa; brief control of ports; rivalry with Ethiopia and European powers.

940.name: French Somaliland
940.description: French acquisition of Obock then Djibouti city; strategic coaling station; Addis Ababa–Djibouti railway; WWII and Cold War developments.

sub_clusters.name: French Acquisition and Obock
sub_clusters.description: France acquires Obock from Afar sultans 1862; establishes Djibouti city 1888 as capital; coal and supply port.

sub_clusters.name: Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway
sub_clusters.description: Franco-Ethiopian railway constructed 1897-1917; transforms Djibouti into Ethiopia's primary trade outlet.

sub_clusters.name: WWII: Vichy then Free France
sub_clusters.description: French Somaliland under Vichy control; British blockade; switches to Free France 1942; famine during blockade.

sub_clusters.name: Referendums and TFAI Period
sub_clusters.description: 1958 and 1967 referendums retain French status; renamed Territory of the Afars and Issas (TFAI) 1967; Issa majority pushes for independence.

950.name: Independence and Gouled Presidency
950.description: Independence 27 June 1977; Hassan Gouled Aptidon's single-party rule; Afar insurgency; limited multiparty opening.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Djibouti
sub_clusters.description: Djibouti gains independence 27 June 1977; Hassan Gouled Aptidon becomes first president; French military remains.

sub_clusters.name: Gouled Single-Party Rule
sub_clusters.description: RPP single-party state; Issa-dominated governance; marginalisation of Afar community; French security guarantee.

sub_clusters.name: Afar Insurgency and Civil Conflict
sub_clusters.description: FRUD (Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy) Afar insurgency; ethnic conflict; 1994 peace accord.

960.name: Guelleh Era and Strategic Hub
960.description: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh's presidency; Djibouti as global military base hub; post-9/11 strategic importance; economic modernisation.

sub_clusters.name: Guelleh Consolidation of Power
sub_clusters.description: Guelleh succeeds Gouled 1999; constitutional amendment removes term limits 2010; opposition suppressed.

sub_clusters.name: Foreign Military Bases
sub_clusters.description: US Camp Lemonnier (2001); French Forces Djibouti; Chinese PLA base (2017, first overseas); Japanese and other installations; rent income.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Modernisation and Port Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Doraleh Container Terminal; new Addis Ababa–Djibouti electric railway (2018); free trade zones; rivalry with Berbera.

sub_clusters.name: Regional Diplomacy and Stability Role
sub_clusters.description: IGAD headquarters; mediation in Somali conflicts; balancing Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Gulf state interests.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
